description:
Add one activeness predicate on `Lease` and three lock-free lease reads in storage, so every lease reader has one path to call.

## Background

Lease activeness is decided in four places with four rules that disagree at `now == expires_at`, and some ignore staleness (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3355-3361`, `commands/template.rs:303`, `commands/validate.rs:2495-2496`, and `Lease::is_expired` at `storage/claim_coordinator.rs:92`). `Lease::is_stale` exists at `:105`. Lock-free readers load the whole index through `ClaimsIndex::load` (`claim_coordinator.rs:210-231`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Lease::is_active(now)` is true when a lease is neither expired nor stale, and one unit test owns its boundaries.
- [hard] REQ-02: `storage/claim_coordinator.rs` offers `read_leases(&WorktreePaths)` (every stored lease), `read_active_leases(&WorktreePaths, now)` and `read_active_lease(&WorktreePaths, &IssueId, now)`, reading without the claims lock, with unit tests.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Storage offers one lock-free lease read path and one activeness rule
